name.en-US: Sts. Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen
name.pt-BR: Santos Basílio Magno e Gregório Nazianzeno

patronOf.en-US: Bishops and doctors of the Church

prayerExcerpt.en-US: We seemed to have one soul, inhabiting two bodies.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Parecíamos ter uma só alma habitando dois corpos.

meta.face: Two clearly different people. Basil: a lean ascetic man in his late forties; a LONG, NARROW face with a high forehead, a long thin aquiline nose with a pronounced bridge, close-set deep-set dark eyes under high-arched black brows, hollow cheeks, thin lips; thick dark hair threaded with grey; a long black beard narrowing to a point. Gregory: a man of about sixty with a BROAD, ROUND, FLESHY face, a short wide nose with a rounded tip, large wide-set soft eyes with heavy lids, full cheeks and a full lower lip; bald crown with a short fringe at the sides; a broad square-cut smoky dark-grey beard; a gentle, meditative look.
meta.basis: The Painter's Manual gives Basil grey hair, a large beard and arched brows, and Gregory baldness and a broad beard 'of a sooty colour'; the Kiev mosaic of Basil and the Chora fresco of Gregory show the same types. Basil is kept dark-haired to separate the pair.
meta.excerpt: Gregory Nazianzen, Oration 43 (on Basil), 20, NPNF 2nd series vol. 7 (1894); pt-BR our rendering
